newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Christian Democrat leaders meet on EU reforms.
newsitem.headline: Christian Democrat leaders meet on EU reforms.

text.p: Centrist leaders from across the European Union said on Wednesday that an ongoing review of the Maastricht Treaty should prepare the bloc for future enlargement and lead to a strong Europe.

"We want a strong Europe. We want enlargement -- the fundamental objective -- to take place in a Europe with precise rules. That implies a reinforcement of the (Maastricht) treaty," Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters.

Prodi was arriving for an evening meeting of the European People's Party (EPP), a grouping of mainly Christian Democrat politicians, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, Luxembourg Premier Jean-Claude Juncker and Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Claude Dehaene.
The EPP leaders routinely meet to coordinate policy ahead of major EU summits.
EU heads of state and government are due to gather for an informal half-day session in the Dutch coastal resort of Noordwijk on Friday to continue preparations for the Amsterdam summit on June 16-17.
An EPP spokesman said that the meeting was likely to be low-key, with the leaders discussing a common position document prepared by EPP staff.
